worn-out.definition: Damaged due to continued or hard exposure or use until no longer effective or useful.

worried.definition: Form of worry (participle past): To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

worries.definition: Form of worry (indicative present singular third-person): To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

worry.definition: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

worrying.definition: Form of worry (gerund participle present): To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

worse.definition: Form of bad (comparative): Of low quality.

worst.definition: Superlative form of bad: most bad.

worthless.definition: Having no worth or use; without value.

would.definition: Past tense of will; usually followed by a bare infinitive.

wounded.definition: Form of wound (participle past): To hurt or injure (someone) by cutting, piercing, or tearing the skin.

wove.definition: Form of weave (past): To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.

wrapped.definition: Form of wrap (participle past): To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.

wrapping.definition: Form of wrap (gerund participle present): To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.

wreak.definition: To cause harm; to afflict; to inflict; to harm or injure; to let out harm.

wreck.definition: Something or someone that has been ruined.

wreckage.definition: Something wrecked, especially the remains or debris of something which has been severely damaged or destroyed.

wrecked.definition: Form of wreck (participle past): To destroy violently; to cause severe damage to something, to a point where it no longer works, or is useless.

wrenched.definition: Form of wrench (participle past): To pull or twist violently.

wrenching.definition: Form of wrench (gerund participle present): To pull or twist violently.

wrests.definition: Form of wrest (indicative present singular third-person): To pull or twist violently.

wriggled.definition: Form of wriggle (participle past): To twist one's body to and fro with short, writhing motions; to squirm.

wringing.definition: Form of wring (gerund participle present): Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.

wrinkled.definition: Form of wrinkle (participle past): To make wrinkles in; to cause to have wrinkles.

wrist.definition: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.

wristwatch.definition: A watch that is worn on a strap or band fastened around the wrist.

write.definition: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

writer.definition: A person who writes, or produces literary work; an author can refer to themselves as "the writer".

writers.definition: Form of writer (plural): A person who writes, or produces literary work; an author can refer to themselves as "the writer".

writhed.definition: Form of writhe (participle past): To twist, wring (something).

written.definition: Form of write (participle past): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

wrongly.definition: In violation of a moral or other standard, code, or convention; in an unfair, unjust, dishonest, or immoral manner; wrongly convicted is synonymous with wrongful conviction and miscarriage of justice.

wrongness.definition: The quality of being wrong; error or fault.

wrote.definition: Form of write (past): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

wrung.definition: Form of wring (participle past): Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.

wry.definition: Turned away, contorted (of the face or body).

wryly.definition: In a wry or sarcastic manner; ironically.

yank.definition: Form of yank (derogatory often): A sudden, vigorous pull (sometimes defined as mass times jerk, or rate of change of force).

yard.definition: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.

yards.definition: Form of yard (plural): A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.

yawn.definition: To open the mouth widely and take a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored, and sometimes accompanied by pandiculation.

yeah.definition: Form of year (colloquial pronunciation-spelling): A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons.

year.definition: Form of here (pronunciation-spelling): This place; this location.

yearn.definition: To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.

yearned.definition: Form of yearn (participle past): To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.

years.definition: Form of year (plural): A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons.

yell.definition: To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice, especially to express intense emotions such as anger or excitement.

yelled.definition: Form of yell (participle past): To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice, especially to express intense emotions such as anger or excitement.

yelling.definition: Form of yell (gerund participle present): To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice, especially to express intense emotions such as anger or excitement.

yellowness.definition: The state, quality, or degree of being yellow in colour.

yelp.definition: An abrupt, high-pitched noise or utterance.

yelped.definition: Form of yelp (participle past): To utter an abrupt, high-pitched noise.

yes.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yesterday.definition: The day immediately before today; one day ago.

yet.definition: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.

yielded.definition: Form of yield (participle past): To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yipped.definition: Form of yip (participle past): to bark with a sharp, high-pitched voice.

yodeled.definition: Form of yodel (participle past): To sing (a song) in such a way that the voice fluctuates rapidly between the normal chest voice and falsetto.

york.definition: To bowl a yorker at a batsman, especially to get a batsman out in this way.

you.definition: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).

young.definition: Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.

younger.definition: Form of young (comparative): In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.

young’s.definition: Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.

youth.definition: The quality or state of being young.

zenith.definition: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.

zero.definition: The numeric symbol that represents the cardinal number zero.

zip.definition: The high-pitched sound of a small object moving rapidly through air.

zipped.definition: Form of zip (participle past): To close with a zip fastener.

zippered.definition: Form of zipper (participle past): To close a zipper.

zooming.definition: Form of zoom (gerund participle present): To move fast with a humming noise.
